newsitem.title: NORWAY: FORECAST - Elkem Q3 pre-tax seen rising.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Elkem Q3 pre-tax seen rising.

text.p: Norwegian metals producer Elkem ASA is expected to book profits before tax of around 781 million crowns for the first nine months, a Reuter poll of seven analysts showed.
In the corresponding year-ago period Elkem posted pre-tax profits of 733 million crowns.
Six of the analysts recommended a buy on Elkem while one said hold. Two of the analysts saying "buy" had upgraded their recommendation in the second quarter from "hold".
The analysts remain positive to the company despite the recent plunge in aluminium prices. Estimates forecast aluminium to average around $1,507 per tonne in 1996 and $1,632 per tonne in 1997.

"There has been a lot of negative sentiment related to aluminium and power, which has been exaggerated. In addition aluminium accounts for only 18 percent of the company's turnover," said one of those polled.

Another analyst said Elkem was undervalued at the current share price of around 90 crowns and saw an upside potential to 120 crowns. An important point was that Elkem would become debt-free during the course of 1998, he said.
"Then we will see a much more shareholder-friendly policy," he said.
Others said the major downside factor was developments in the manganese and chrome sectors.
"I think income in manganese and chrome will be worse than market expectations. Chrome prices have fallen hard and fast," said another analyst.
Elkem will present nine-month results at 1300 GMT on October 22. Following lists analysts' expectations.
